H_hierarchical.evidence: Paper states three control modes and that each mode is governed by its own FSM managing flight-phase transitions.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Figure/control text includes multiple meaningful guards such as Land?, Finish explore (time), Corner Detection/No Corner, and dceil <= tol / dceil > tol.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Mission actions include takeoff, record data, compute open-space vector and velocity command, adjust attitude, maintain altitude/distance, update altitude, and move the robot.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: Requirements and control text specify manual fallback during autonomy failure, hardware kill switch, and that the operator can take control or land at any moment.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Safety recovery appears in the data-collection pipeline, failure fallback/kill switch in requirements, and mission-state behavior in Section 3.5/Figure 6.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as safety recovery, manual control fallback, hardware kill switch, and safe altitude imply control rules beyond a flat state list.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Figure 6 names states like Free Space, V_cmd, Corner Detection, and Update altitude, while the associated computations/actions are described later in prose and equations.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The paper gives arithmetic for velocity computation, but explicit transition guards are mainly simple event/time/threshold conditions.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: The paper defines per-mode FSMs, but does not clearly assign separate entry/during/exit behavior to a parent composite state beyond its substates.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The operator can take control or land the UAV at any moment, and autonomy failure triggers manual fallback.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is a shallow hierarchical mission selector with three mode-specific FSMs and an initial data-recording/mission-selection path.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: No clear set of arithmetic-plus-boolean transition guards where SMT-style consistency checking would be central.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Manual override/landing applies cross-cuttingly across autonomous substates, and mission modes include continuous maintenance of altitude or inspection distance.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Some side effects are abstract mission outputs such as record data and monitor status, while many actions are concrete UAV commands.

key_nl_quotes: Each mode is governed by its own FSM, which manages transitions between flight phases, ensuring safety and data integrity.
the operator can take control or land the UAV at any moment
one_line_pitch: A hierarchical UAV mission supervisor with mode-specific FSMs, computed control actions, threshold/event guards, and global manual-recovery paths stresses exactly the hierarchy, action, guard, and escape-pattern weaknesses of Umple-style baselines.
rationale: The sample is a strong stress test because the paper provides an explicit hierarchical mission architecture: a top-level mission selector branches into manual logging, reactive exploration, and supervised pillar inspection, each with its own FSM. The stress comes less from dense arithmetic guards than from attributing prose-defined actions to figure-defined states, preserving mode hierarchy, and encoding global manual fallback/landing behavior across many autonomous substates. It has enough concrete state, guard, action, and recovery evidence to build a reference state machine without being too thin.
